results.note: Read Router.app: the alternate-slash redirect (lines 714-728) and every skip condition (non-http type, redirect_slashes false, route_path == '/', any route already matching, no route matching the alternate form) live in this one method. redirect_slashes is only stored in Router.__init__, not evaluated there; the query does not ask how to disable it.

Route.matches returns Match.PARTIAL on path hit with wrong verb; Router.app keeps the first partial and dispatches it only after no FULL match; Route.handle builds the Allow header and raises/returns 405. ExceptionMiddleware.http_exception only forwards exc.headers and was judged not essential. HTTPEndpoint.method_not_allowed is a different path (class endpoints give a FULL match) and the query's 'half-existing address / who picks among candidates' wording fits only the Route path.

stream() replays a cached _body but raises RuntimeError('Stream consumed') when _stream_consumed is set and no _body exists; body() is the only place that fills _body (by draining stream()). Both bodies needed to explain the asymmetry.

Only place choosing MultiPartParser vs FormParser vs empty FormData from the parsed Content-Type (grep for the two media types hits requests.py only). Request.form is a thin wrapper and does not decide.

_parse_range_header returns [] when range_.count(',')+1 > cls.max_ranges (100); __call__ maps len(ranges)==0 to _handle_simple (whole file, self.status_code). max_ranges is a class attribute, not an entity. _handle_simple only streams and was judged not needed.

preflight_response collects failures (origin, method, headers, private-network) and builds 'Disallowed CORS ...' with status 400; is_allowed_origin implements the origin check (wildcard, regex fullmatch, list). CORSMiddleware.__call__ only routes to preflight_response and is not needed for the question.

Cookie is written only when session.modified (send_wrapper in __call__); Session overrides every mutator to call mark_modified. HTTPConnection.session calls mark_accessed, but 'accessed' only drives the Vary: Cookie header, not whether a cookie is sent, so it was not added; a reader who takes 'touched' to include reads could argue for it (borderline, not required).

GZipMiddleware.__call__ reads Accept-Encoding and picks GZipResponder vs IdentityResponder. All skip rules (content-encoding already set, status 206, excluded media type incl. wildcard and grpc+, body < minimum_size) are in the inherited IdentityResponder.send_with_compression, which GZipResponder reuses. GZipResponder.apply_compression has no skip rule.

'No response returned.' is raised only at base.py:180 inside the nested call_next defined in __call__, on anyio.EndOfStream with app_exc None (inner app returned without sending http.response.start; coro closes send_stream). Grep confirms a single raise site.

lookup_path uses realpath (symlinks resolved) unless follow_symlink, then commonpath != directory -> continue -> ('', None); __init__ accepts follow_symlink. The 404 itself is raised in StaticFiles.get_response when stat_result is None; judged not necessary because the query asks which check blocks and which option disables it, not where the 404 is raised (borderline).

Response.__call__ sends start and body then awaits self.background(); BackgroundTasks.__call__ loops tasks sequentially in insertion order; BackgroundTask.__call__ awaits async funcs and uses run_in_threadpool for sync ones. concurrency.run_in_threadpool is a two-line anyio wrapper already named in the BackgroundTask body, so not added (optional).

build_middleware_stack puts ServerErrorMiddleware first (outermost), then optional body limit, then user_middleware, then ExceptionMiddleware last (innermost), wrapping router via reversed loop; add_middleware does user_middleware.insert(0, ...) so later additions become outermost among user layers.

__call__ matches host == pattern or pattern startswith '*' and host endswith pattern[1:]; found_www_redirect set when 'www.'+host == pattern; redirects only if www_redirect true, else 400. __init__ only validates/normalizes patterns and stores the flag.

Single raise site (grep 'already started'): nested wrapped_app inside wrap_app_handling_exceptions raises when an exception has a registered handler (status or class lookup) after sender saw http.response.start. ServerErrorMiddleware tracks response_started too but does not raise this error.

Traceback line 153 matches the raise in compile_path. Besides duplicates it asserts convertor type is in CONVERTOR_TYPES ('Unknown path convertor'); it also builds regex/format/convertor map and strips port for host patterns. Callers (Route.__init__ etc.) are not needed.

Traceback lines 125 and 63 match receive_text and the else-branch raise in receive. First disconnect sets client_state to DISCONNECTED (line 60) while application_state stays CONNECTED, so receive_text's guard passes on the next call and receive raises WebSocketDisconnected. _raise_on_disconnect explains why the first disconnect surfaced as WebSocketDisconnect but is not needed to answer 'what state makes it fail'.
Assertion at requests.py:172 checks 'session' in self.scope; only SessionMiddleware.__call__ assigns scope['session'] (and skips scope types other than http/websocket).

__setitem__ keeps the first matching entry (overwritten in place) and deletes the other duplicates; append adds without touching existing entries. Response.headers returns MutableHeaders, so assignment routes here; update() also calls __setitem__.

added.reason: HTTPConnection.url_for only delegates; the construction of the complete URL (scheme from protocol and base_url.is_secure, netloc, base path + route path) is done in make_absolute_url, which the query explicitly asks about ('come costruisce l'indirizzo completo').

results.note: _setup_env_defaults registers the url_for global reading context['request']; TemplateResponse does context.setdefault('request', request); url_for resolves the name through router.url_path_for and calls make_absolute_url with self.base_url.

ServerErrorMiddleware.__call__ sends the 500 then 'raise exc' (comment says test clients may re-raise); in handle_request the nested close_app re-raises app_task.exception() when raise_server_exceptions is true. TestClient.__init__ only forwards the flag; the query asks for 'two parts'.

get_schema 'if not parsed: continue' drops endpoints with empty parsed docstring; parse_docstring splits on '---' taking the last part, yaml.safe_load, returns {} unless a dict. get_endpoints drops other routes (include_in_schema, HEAD) but not on docstring grounds.

__getitem__ adds key to _has_been_read; __setitem__/__delitem__ raise EnvironError if the key was read. Config.get reads via the Environ and thus triggers the record but is the consumer, not the guard.

dispatch maps HEAD to 'get' when no 'head' attribute and checks membership in _allowed_methods; __init__ builds _allowed_methods (HEAD counted when 'get' exists); method_not_allowed builds Allow and raises/returns 405.

In requires the async/sync wrappers redirect (303, ?next=<url>) when redirect is not None, otherwise raise HTTPException(status_code); has_required_scope checks every scope is in conn.auth.scopes. The websocket branch just closes.
